sources.entry: PicoShare - Minimalist, easy-to-host service for sharing images and other files. (Clients) AGPL-3.0 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: PicoShare is a minimalist, self-hosted web app for sharing files of any type and size through direct download links.
summary.what_it_does: PicoShare runs as a self-hosted web service, started from Go source or a Docker image. It gives each uploaded file a direct download link that anyone can view or download without ads or signups. It does not resize or re-encode uploaded media, so links are available as soon as the upload finishes. Data is stored in a SQLite database, which can optionally be replicated to Litestream-compatible cloud storage and restored on container restart. Access is controlled by an admin passphrase set through an environment variable or a secret file. Configuration covers the listening port, reverse-proxy logging, and the database path.
use_cases: Share large or unusual files with someone via a direct link
Self-host a private file sharing service
Send images, video, or audio without re-encoding or resizing
Run a simple file host on a cloud platform such as fly.io
Back up a small SQLite-based app to S3-compatible storage with Litestream
how_to_run: Optional: set LITESTREAM_BUCKET, LITESTREAM_ENDPOINT, LITESTREAM_ACCESS_KEY_ID and LITESTREAM_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY to replicate data to cloud storage
Or use the provided docker-compose.yml with docker-compose up
notable: Direct download links with no signups, ads, or file type or size limits
Never resizes or re-encodes uploaded media
Optional Litestream replication of the SQLite database to Litestream-compatible cloud storage
Single-container deployment with a mounted volume for data
caveats: Only one Docker container should run per Litestream location, since writes cannot sync across instances
Deleted files do not free disk space automatically; the SQLite database must be vacuumed manually while PicoShare is stopped
Maintained by one person as a hobby project with a deliberately limited feature scope
